newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tankers little changed in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tankers little changed in thin market.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were steady to slightly lower on Wednesday in a quiet market, brokers said.
Rates for VLCCs out of the Middle East to Japan were steady but risked weakening if the market continued its recent lacklustre performance, brokers said.

In that sector, the 250,000 tonne World Pendant was reported chartered by Petrodiamond for a trip from Mina al Bakr to Japan at a rate of W62.5 loading March 12, while the 240,000 tonne Navix Adventure was fixed by Mobil for Middle East-Japan at W60.
"We could see it coming off a bit," said one broker. "But its not unusual for it to be quiet at this time of the month."
The UK-continent sector, which has saw a flurry of end-of-month fixing at the beginning of the week, was fairly steady with 80,000 tonne vessels commanding between W107.5-110.

Brokers said a number of charterers had expressed interest in transatlantic vessels - with Bayway reported to have fixed a vessel the 80,000 tonne SCF Star for a trip from the North Sea to the US Atlantic coast loading March 6.
The West Africa sector was fairly firm with 130,000 tonners bound for the United States commanding around W85-90 depending on the quality of the vessel.
In the Mediterranean market, 130,000 tonners were fixed at around W82.5-85 and 80,000 tonners commanded around W115-117.50.
The Caribbean remained under pressure, with 70,000 tonners doing the up U.S. coast trip commanding around W115.
